notes: Built from a60-required-meaning-01 and a60-recommended-meaning-01 (turn 1) and sc-required-definition-01, sc-recommended-definition-01, sc-nfm-mandate-01 (turn 2). Definitional control: the question is what two words mean as terms of art, not what any single procedure is. Both chapters carry the same front-matter definition, so the answer is short, redundant across the corpus and easy for any arm that retrieves either chapter - hence 'tie'. Slice check: this is the strongest slice-immune definitional topic available. The operator source-of-truth and the four probe datasheets contain no notion of 'required' versus 'recommended' as graded obligations, and no notion of documenting a departure - grep of SLICE-EXCLUSION for 'required'/'recommend' returns only Atlas Scientific product suggestions (cable isolators, probe cleaner, reconditioning kit), which is a different sense of the word entirely. An arm restricted to the slice cannot answer either turn.

turns.content: Reading through these chapters, some steps are flagged as required and others as recommended. Practically speaking, what's the difference in what we have to do?

must_contain: states that 'required' marks established policy, settled by research or by technical consensus among specialists, and is to be followed as written
states that 'recommended' means more than one acceptable way of doing it exists
states that when a recommended step is involved, the reason for picking the option you picked has to be written down
must_not: treats the two words as interchangeable emphasis or as stylistic wording
claims 'recommended' means optional and needs no record
invents a third category or a numeric grading scheme

turns.content: And if a site just won't let us do the required one - no room for the gear, say - is it enough to note it in the log and move on?

must_contain: states that a departure from a required procedure has to be documented
states that documenting is not sufficient on its own - the departure also has to be independently quality assured
notes that the same documentation-plus-independent-quality-assurance expectation applies to departures from recommended procedures
must_not: says a note in the field log by itself closes the matter
invents a specific USGS form, approval chain, or sign-off role for the departure
claims required procedures can never be departed from under any circumstances
